([[Columbus, Mississippi]]) | college = [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] (2018–2020) | highlights = | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|2015 Argentina]] | [[United States men's national under-16 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Robert Anthony Woodard II''' (born September 22, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. ==Early life and high school career== Woodard grew up playing [[basketball]] and [[baseball]] but narrowed his focus to basketball by the time he started high school, in part due to his exceptional height.{{cite web |last1=Lowery |first1=Logan |title=Woodard's basketball focus paying off |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/woodard-s-basketball-focus-paying-off/article_f4f33ddd-5511-58d8-8f08-23868876d8d5.html |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2019}} He was already receiving Division I college attention in eighth grade. He played basketball for [[Columbus High School (Mississippi)|Columbus High School]] in [[Columbus, Mississippi]].{{cite web |last1=Faulk |first1=Robbie |title=Robert Woodard Sr. "Elated" in Son's Decision |url=https://247sports.com/college/mississippi-state/Article/Robert-Woodard-Sr-Elated-in-Sons-Decision-110634869/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=November 24, 2017}} As a sophomore, Woodard led Columbus to its first Mississippi Class 6A state title after averaging 20.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and four assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Sammon |first1=Will |title=Luther Riley out as Columbus basketball coach |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/06/10/luther-riley-out-columbus-basketball-coach/85641382/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=June 10, 2016}} In his junior season, he averaged 25.2 points, 13.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists and three blocks per game and was named Mississippi [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Costabile |first1=Annie |title=Robert Woodard named Gatorade POY |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/03/20/columbus-robert-woodard-named-gatorade-player-year/99422174/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=March 20, 2017}} As a senior, Woodard won his second Class 6A state championship and repeated as Mississippi Gatorade Player of the Year. A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the highest-rated prospect in his state, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], among others.{{cite web |title=Four-star forward Robert Woodard commits to Mississippi State |url=https://www.wjtv.com/sports/four-star-forward-robert-woodard-commits-to-mississippi-state/ |website=[[WJTV]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=November 15, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman, Woodard averaged 5.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game in 17.4 minutes per game. He started one contest and shot 46 percent on field goals. He spent the following summer working on his shooting and lifting weights. On November 17, 2019, Woodard set career highs with 21 points and 16 rebounds in a 82–59 win over [[New Orleans Privateers men's basketball|New Orleans]].{{cite news |title=Woodard sends Mississippi State past New Orleans 82-59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169835 |accessdate=December 25, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 17, 2019}} As a sophomore, Woodard averaged 11.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=S. Carolina, Miss. St. meet in conference play |url=https://apnews.com/bcbee7cc70104514b9036046d7617687 |accessdate=March 19, 2020 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 18, 2020}} Following the season, Woodard declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], with the intention of remaining in the draft.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Mississippi State's Robert Woodard II entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29016177/mississippi-state-robert-woodard-ii-entering-nba-draft |accessdate=April 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 9, 2020}} He had a career total of 539 points, 53 steals, 49 blocks, 65 assists and 342 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Lydia |title=From MSU to the NBA: Robert Woodard II |url=http://www.reflector-online.com/sports/article_7ec32e4a-f51d-11ea-b04d-3b88334598bf.html |accessdate=October 5, 2020 |work=The Reflector |date=September 13, 2020}} ==National team career== Woodard won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national under-16 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] in [[Bahía Blanca]], Argentina. He played in all five games and averaged 5.6 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Cronin |first1=Courtney |title=Woodard, USA Basketball win gold at FIBA Americas |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/prepsreport/2015/06/15/robert-woodard-fiba-americas/71253188/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |date=June 15, 2015}} ==Career
